newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. may issue 10-year visas to India travellers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may issue 10-year visas to India travellers.

text.p: The United States may soon issue visas valid for 10 years to Indian businessmen and tourists travelling there, the United News of India (UNI) agency reported on Wednesday.
UNI quoted U.S. Assistant Secretary of Consular Affairs Mary Ryan as saying that she had discussed the subject with officials of India's External Affairs Ministry.
"The five years' visa to Indian nationals is on a reciprocal basis," UNI quoted Ryan as telling a news conference.
"Since India is now switching over to a 10-year and 20-year passport system, we may start giving ten years' visas to Indian tourists and businessmen."
Ryan added, "We don't want to see them standing in the queue for visas again and again."

Ryan said 151,000 Indian nationals were issued U.S. visas last year, an increase of 34 percent over the previous year's figures. She expected the number of visa applicants from India to rise to 500,000 by the year 2001, UNI added.
